hook.en: A study says people who exercise live longer. But exercisers also smoke less, eat better and earn more. Regression is the tool that tries to separate these threads, and it is also easy to misuse. Learn what it can and cannot do.
hook.ur: Study kehti hai exercise karne walay zyada jeete hain. Lekin exercise karne walay cigarette kam peete, behtar khate aur zyada kamate hain. Regression woh aala hai jo in dhagon ko alag karne ki koshish karta hai, aur ismein ghalat istemal bhi aasaan hai. Seekhein yeh kya kar sakta hai aur kya nahi.

goal.en: By the end, you'll explain what linear and logistic regression do, define a confounder and how adjustment works, read a regression coefficient or an odds ratio in plain words, and spot common errors such as too many variables and adjusting for the wrong thing.
goal.ur: End tak aap samjhayenge ke linear aur logistic regression kya karte hain, confounder aur adjustment ki tareef karenge, regression coefficient ya odds ratio saade alfaaz mein parhenge, aur aam ghaltiyan pehchanenge jaise bohat zyada variables aur ghalat cheez ko adjust karna.

text.en: **Regression** describes how an outcome changes with one or more predictors, while holding the others constant. **Linear regression** is for a continuous outcome and gives a **coefficient**: the average change in the outcome for a one-unit change in the predictor. **Logistic regression** is for a yes-or-no outcome and gives an **odds ratio**. A **confounder** is related to both the exposure and the outcome and is not on the causal path between them. **Adjustment** adds the confounder to the model so its effect is accounted for.
text.ur: **Regression** batata hai ke nateeja ek ya zyada predictors ke saath kaise badalta hai, baqi ko mustaqil rakhte hue. **Linear regression** continuous nateeje ke liye hai aur **coefficient** deta hai: predictor mein ek unit tabdeeli par nateeje mein average tabdeeli. **Logistic regression** haan ya nahi nateeje ke liye hai aur **odds ratio** deta hai. **Confounder** exposure aur nateeje dono se juda hota hai aur dono ke beech wajah ke raaste par nahi hota. **Adjustment** confounder ko model mein jorta hai taake us ka asar hisab mein aa jaye.

text.en: Think of **comparing two runners**. One is faster, but also younger and trained longer. To judge the shoes they wear, you need to compare runners of the same age and training. Regression does this "matching" with statistics, comparing like with like. But it can only match on the things you measured.
text.ur: **Do dauriyon ka muqabla** sochein. Ek tez hai, lekin jawan bhi hai aur zyada der se training karta hai. Un ke jootay parakhne ke liye aap ko ek hi umar aur training ke daurne walon ka muqabla chahiye. Regression yeh "milana" shumariyat se karta hai, barabar se barabar ka muqabla. Lekin yeh sirf un cheezon par mila sakta hai jo aap ne naapin.

title.en: Common regression types and how to read them
title.ur: Aam regression ki qismein aur unhein kaise parhein

rows.en: "Each extra year of age was associated with 0.3 points more pain, after adjusting for sex"
rows.ur: "Har aik saal ki umar 0.3 point zyada dard se juda thi, jins ko adjust karne ke baad"

rows.en: Yes or no (for example, returned to work)
rows.ur: Haan ya nahi (masalan kaam par wapas aaya)

rows.en: "An odds ratio of 2.0 means the odds of returning to work were twice as high"
rows.ur: "2.0 ka odds ratio matlab kaam par wapas aane ke odds dugne thay"

rows.en: Time until an event (for example, time to re-injury)
rows.ur: Waqt jab tak koi waqia ho (masalan dobara chot lagne tak waqt)

rows.en: "A hazard ratio of 0.7 means a 30 percent lower rate of re-injury at any time"
rows.ur: "0.7 ka hazard ratio matlab kisi bhi waqt dobara chot ki sharah 30 fisad kam"

question.en: A study finds that patients who attend more physiotherapy sessions have worse outcomes. A reviewer suggests the sicker patients may attend more sessions. What is this?
question.ur: Study paati hai ke zyada physiotherapy sessions mein aane wale mareezon ke nateeje buray hain. Ek reviewer kehta hai ke zyada bimar mareez zyada sessions mein aate honge. Yeh kya hai?

text.en: Selection bias in a randomised trial
Confounding by indication: severity affects both the number of sessions and the outcome
text.ur: Confounding by indication: shiddat sessions ki ginti aur nateeje dono ko mutasir karti hai

feedback.en: Yes — baseline severity must be adjusted for.
feedback.ur: Haan — shuruaati shiddat ko adjust karna hoga.

feedback.en: The main issue is a shared cause.

question.en: A model with 8 predictors is fitted to 40 patients. What is the problem?
question.ur: 40 mareezon par 8 predictors wala model fit kiya gaya. Masla kya hai?

text.en: Nothing, more predictors are always better
text.ur: Kuch nahi, zyada predictors hamesha behtar hain

text.en: Overfitting: too few events or patients per variable, so the model fits noise and will not replicate
text.ur: Overfitting: har variable ke liye bohat kam events ya mareez, isliye model shor ko fit karta hai aur dohraya nahi ja sakta

feedback.en: Yes — a common rule of thumb is about 10 events or patients per predictor.
feedback.ur: Haan — aam andaaze ka qaida har predictor ke liye takreeban 10 events ya mareez hai.

feedback.en: It is too complex for the sample.
feedback.ur: Sample ke liye bohat pechida hai.

question.en: Which of these should you NOT adjust for in a study of whether a treatment reduces pain?
question.ur: Ilaaj dard kam karta hai ya nahi ke study mein in mein se kis ko adjust NAHI karna chahiye?

feedback.en: Sex is a reasonable adjustment variable.

text.en: Age and baseline pain measured before treatment
text.ur: Umar aur ilaaj se pehle naapa gaya baseline dard

feedback.en: Baseline variables are sensible to adjust for.
feedback.ur: Baseline variables adjust karna samajhdari hai.

text.en: A variable that lies on the causal path from treatment to pain, such as the improved strength produced by the treatment
text.ur: Woh variable jo ilaaj se dard tak wajah ke raaste par ho, jaise ilaaj se paida hone wali behtar taqat

feedback.en: Yes — adjusting for a mediator removes part of the effect you want to measure.
feedback.ur: Haan — mediator ko adjust karne se woh asar kam ho jata hai jo aap naapna chahte hain.

text.en: **Believing that adjustment removes all confounding.** Adjustment only handles confounders that you measured, and measured well. Unmeasured confounders remain. Another trap is adjusting for everything available, including mediators and colliders, which can distort results; choose variables with a causal diagram (a simple drawing of arrows) before running the model. And do not say "causes" from an adjusted observational analysis alone.
text.ur: **Yeh samajhna ke adjustment saari confounding hata deta hai.** Adjustment sirf un confounders ko sambhalta hai jo aap ne naape, aur achhi tarah naape. Na-naape confounders rehte hain. Ek aur jaal har dastiyab cheez ko adjust karna hai, mediators aur colliders samet, jo nateejon ko bigad sakta hai; model chalane se pehle causal diagram (teeron ki saadi tasveer) se variables chunein. Aur sirf adjusted observational tajziye se "wajah hai" na kahein.

text.en: **Draw before you model.** Sketch boxes and arrows: exposure, outcome and the other factors. Ask which arrows point into both exposure and outcome (confounders), and which lie in between (mediators). It takes five minutes and prevents the most common modelling mistakes. Share your diagram in the methods section.
text.ur: **Model se pehle tasveer banayein.** Dibbe aur teer banayein: exposure, nateeja aur doosre factors. Poochhein kaun se teer exposure aur nateeje dono mein jate hain (confounders), aur kaun beech mein hain (mediators). Yeh paanch minute leta hai aur modelling ki sab se aam ghaltiyon se bachata hai. Apna diagram methods section mein share karein.

question.en: Does a significant regression coefficient mean the predictor causes the outcome?
question.ur: Kya significant regression coefficient ka matlab predictor nateeje ki wajah hai?

answer.en: No. Regression describes association, even after adjustment. Causation also requires a plausible mechanism, correct time order, no important unmeasured confounding, and ideally replication or randomisation. A randomised trial is stronger because randomisation balances both measured and unmeasured factors. Regression in a trial is still useful for precision and for checking balance.
answer.ur: Nahi. Regression adjustment ke baad bhi association bayan karta hai. Wajah ke liye mumkina tareeqa-e-kaar, sahi waqt ki tarteeb, koi ahem na-naapa confounding na ho, aur behtar dohrana ya randomisation bhi chahiye. Randomised trial mazboot hai kyunke randomisation naape aur na-naape dono factors ko mutawazin karti hai. Trial mein regression phir bhi durusti aur balance jaanchne ke liye mufeed hai.

beats.patient: A cohort study of 500 runners finds that those who stretch before running have fewer injuries (odds ratio 0.7). The researchers adjust for age, sex and weekly distance.
beats.assessment: The adjusted result shows a lower odds of injury among stretchers, but runners who stretch may also be more careful, wear better shoes or have coaches, none of which were measured.
beats.treatment: She reads the estimate as "associated with", notes the unmeasured factors, and does not recommend stretching as an injury-prevention treatment on this evidence alone.
beats.reassess: She waits for randomised trials and meanwhile tells runners that stretching is fine if they enjoy it but its injury-prevention benefit is unproven.

text.en: **Adjusted results can still hide harm.** If an observational study suggests a medicine or technique is linked with harm, adjustment may reduce or hide the signal when the true cause is complex. Do not dismiss a safety signal because the adjusted p-value is above 0.05; look at the size and direction of the estimate and its interval.
text.ur: **Adjusted nateeje phir bhi nuqsan chhupa sakte hain.** Agar observational study ishara kare ke dawai ya technique nuqsan se juda hai to jab asal wajah pechida ho adjustment ishare ko kam ya chhupa sakta hai. Safety ke ishaare ko is liye radd na karein ke adjusted p-value 0.05 se oopar hai; andaaze ka size, rukh aur interval dekhein.

text.en: Greenland, Pearl and Robins showed how causal diagrams help investigators decide which variables to adjust for, by encoding assumptions about causes and showing which sets of variables remove confounding without introducing bias. Regression textbooks note that the number of predictors should be limited relative to the number of events or participants to avoid overfitting, with rough rules of about 10 events per variable for logistic or Cox models, and that these rules are guides, not guarantees.
text.ur: Greenland, Pearl aur Robins ne dikhaya ke causal diagrams muhaqqiqon ko kaise madad karte hain ke kaun se variables adjust karein, wajuhaat ke baare mein assumptions encode kar ke aur yeh dikha kar ke variables ke kaun se set bias paida kiye baghair confounding hataate hain. Regression ki kitabein batati hain ke overfitting se bachne ke liye predictors ki ginti events ya shirkat karne walon ke muqabale mein mehdood honi chahiye, logistic ya Cox models ke liye takreeban har variable par 10 events ke andaze ke saath, aur yeh qaide rehnumai hain, zamanat nahi.

text.en: **Draw, Adjust the common cause, Not the middle.** Draw the causes, adjust for common causes (confounders) and not for things in the middle (mediators).
text.ur: **Banayein, Mushtarak wajah ko adjust, Beech wale ko nahi.** Wajuhaat ki tasveer banayein, mushtarak wajuhaat (confounders) ko adjust karein aur beech ki cheezon (mediators) ko nahi.

summary.en: Regression describes an outcome in relation to predictors, and adjustment accounts for measured confounders.
summary.ur: Regression nateeje ko predictors ke saath bayan karta hai, aur adjustment naape gaye confounders ko hisab mein laata hai.

summary.en: Do not adjust for mediators, do not overfit and remember unmeasured confounders remain.
summary.ur: Mediators ko adjust na karein, overfit na karein aur yaad rakhein ke na-naape confounders baqi rehte hain.

summary.en: Draw a causal diagram before modelling and use "associated with" for observational results.
summary.ur: Modelling se pehle causal diagram banayein aur observational nateejon ke liye "se juda" istemal karein.

back.en: A factor related to both exposure and outcome, not on the causal path.
back.ur: Exposure aur nateeje dono se juda factor jo wajah ke raaste par na ho.

front.en: What does an odds ratio of 2 mean?
front.ur: 2 ke odds ratio ka matlab kya hai?

back.en: The odds of the outcome are twice as high in one group as in the other.
back.ur: Ek group mein nateeje ke odds doosre se dugne hain.

back.en: A model that fits noise in the data and will not replicate.
back.ur: Aisa model jo data ke shor ko fit kare aur dohraya na ja sake.

front.en: Should you adjust for a mediator?
front.ur: Kya mediator ko adjust karna chahiye?

back.en: No; it removes part of the effect you want to measure.
back.ur: Nahi; yeh woh asar kam kar deta hai jo aap naapna chahte hain.
